items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: So, we organized this group with his wife playing drums and him playing piano... And we played service clubs... this Bill Williams, he wouldn't take any money... Well, that man had so much confidence in me and enjoyed it so much, he went out and bought a cabaret... now put your band in.

ctx.x: Right, I want to touch up on a lot of things as we go along.

Yeah. Fletcher was a very important thing in what happened, because his first band was an eight-piece band -- we traveled on the road with Ethel Waters, did one nighters and also week stands at the TOBA Time, you know, black circuit. And in that band we had practically the same bunch out of Leroy's cabaret, plus more, and we had a baritone player from Memphis and Bill ? I remember. And we did that tour with Ethel Waters. And Fletcher then -- after we did that tour Fletcher came back and worked at a place called…
